connections.why: Requirements are clarified by analysing how existing products perform
Insights from existing products feed idea generation and communication
Sustainability and ethical issues affect whether a solution is viable
Material choice determines which manufacturing processes are usable
Technical understanding explains why materials behave as they do
Each manufacturing process carries specific health and safety controls
Material and cost factors decide the viability of a solution
Design thinking skills are applied to generate and develop proposals
Knowing how to identify requirements is the basis for analysing a context
Core technical principles are the toolkit applied to problems
Maths and science underpin technical problem-solving
Proposals are tested against viability criteria
Context-analysis skills drive the Explore stage of the NEA
Proposal-development skills feed the Create stage of the NEA
Viability evaluation underpins the Evaluate stage of the NEA
Understanding requirements directs what is created and prototyped
Prototypes are then tested and evaluated against the brief
Evaluation findings feed back into the next iteration of the design
Knowledge of processes enables effective prototyping in the NEA
